# Command reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_cli_docs.py from the parser of `sf`. Do not edit by hand:
     change the command's definition in superfarm/cli/ and run
     `python scripts/gen_cli_docs.py -o docs/CLI.md`. -->

For anyone who runs the farm from a terminal or a script. Every command of `sf`, with its usage,
options and an example. `sf <command> --help` prints the same text for one command.

## Conventions

`sf` has two kinds of commands. Local commands (`doctor`, `host`, `config`, `token`, `serve`,
`service`, `version`, `completion`) work on the machine and need no daemon. All others talk to
the daemon over HTTP, so the daemon must be running (`sf serve` or `sf service start`).

A selector picks Androids. It is one of `all`, `running`, `stopped`, `tag:NAME`, a number such
as `5`, or a range such as `1-10`. Join selectors with commas and exclude with `!`, for example
`1-10,tag:eu,!tag:spare`.

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 the operation failed, 2 wrong usage, 130 interrupted with Ctrl-C. `sf doctor` exits 1 when a check fails, and `sf service status` exits 3 when the service is not active.

The global options below are accepted before and after the command name (`sf --json ls` and
`sf ls --json` are the same).

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--home DIR` | farm home to work on (default: $SUPERFARM_HOME or ~/.local/share/superfarm) |
| `--json` | print the result as JSON (for scripts) |
| `--wait, --no-wait` | follow a started task to its end and show per-device results (default: yes on a terminal, no in a script) |
| `-q, --quiet` | no progress line and no hints, only the result |

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sf ls` (`list`) | list the Androids and their state |
| `sf create` | add Androids (they are created stopped) |
| `sf start` | start Androids |
| `sf restart` | restart Androids |
| `sf recreate` | rebuild the containers of Androids (data is kept) |
| `sf stop` | stop Androids |
| `sf rm` (`delete`) | delete Androids (asks first) |
| `sf set` | change settings of Androids (applied at their next restart) |
| `sf info` | show one Android in detail |
| `sf logs` | show the container logs of one Android |
| `sf gpu` | GPUs and the rendering mode of Androids |
| `sf image` | Android images, one per Android version |
| `sf tasks` | list background tasks, or show, follow and cancel one |
| `sf top` | live load of the host, the GPUs and every running Android |
| `sf open` | print the panel's address and how to log in |
| `sf shell` | run a command inside Androids |
| `sf screenshot` | save a screenshot of one Android |
| `sf apps` | the app library: APK / XAPK / APKS / APKM files kept by the farm |
| `sf app` | apps on the Androids: install, launch, stop, clear, compare versions |
| `sf push` | copy a local file onto Androids |
| `sf pull` | copy a file from one Android to this machine |
| `sf gallery` | add a picture or video to the gallery of Androids |
| `sf input` | send the same touch or key to many Androids at once |
| `sf window` | native device windows (scrcpy) on the desktop the daemon runs on |
| `sf vpn` | VPN profiles, logins and tunnel status |
| `sf gateway` | shared VPN gateways: one tunnel for many Androids |
| `sf camera` | feed a video or live stream into the camera and microphone of Androids |
| `sf listen` | hear one Android on the speakers of the machine the daemon runs on |
| `sf auto` | automation: train recordings into programs and run programs or flows |
| `sf backup` | back up and restore Androids and the farm's settings |
| `sf mcp` | let MCP-enabled AI assistants see and operate the farm |
| `sf approvals` | answer AI assistants that ask to change the farm |
| `sf ask` | ask the built-in Assistant to look at or operate the farm |
| `sf ai` | the in-farm AI: model profiles, the Assistant, the Pilot |
| `sf doctor` | check that this machine can run Androids, with the fix for each problem |
| `sf host` | prepare and inspect this machine (kernel modules, limits, GPUs) |
| `sf config` | read and change the farm's settings (config.yaml) |
| `sf token` | print the API token the panel and scripts log in with |
| `sf serve` | run the daemon (panel + API) in the foreground |
| `sf service` | run the daemon as a systemd user service |
| `sf version` | print the version |
| `sf completion` | print a shell completion script |

## sf ls

Alias: `sf list`.

List the Androids and their state.

```
sf ls [-w] [--interval SECONDS]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-w, --watch` |  | keep the list on screen and refresh it |
| `--interval SECONDS` | `2.0` | refresh interval for -w (default: 2) |

Example:

```
sf ls
sf ls -w
```

## sf create

Add one or more Androids. Anything not given follows the farm's settings (sf config show) and keeps following them when they change.

```
sf create [-n COUNT] [--name NAME] [--android VERSION]
          [--gpu {auto,software,igpu,dgpu,intel,amd,nvidia}]
          [--net {direct,vpn,gateway,proxy,none}] [--vpn PROFILE] [--gateway NAME] [--cpus CPUS]
          [--memory MIB] [--width WIDTH] [--height HEIGHT] [--dpi DPI] [--fps FPS] [--tag TAG]
          [--data-volume VOLUME] [--image IMAGE]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-n, --count COUNT` | `1` | how many (default: 1) |
| `--name NAME` |  | display name (numbered when several are created) |
| `--android VERSION` |  | Android version, e.g. 13 (default: android.default_version) |
| `--gpu {auto,software,igpu,dgpu,intel,amd,nvidia}` |  | rendering: CPU only (software), integrated or discrete GPU, a vendor, or auto |
| `--net {direct,vpn,gateway,proxy,none}` |  | network mode |
| `--vpn PROFILE` |  | pin this VPN profile (implies --net vpn) |
| `--gateway NAME` |  | shared VPN gateway to use (implies --net gateway) |
| `--cpus CPUS` |  | CPU cores each may use |
| `--memory MIB` |  | RAM limit each, in MiB |
| `--width WIDTH` |  | screen width in pixels |
| `--height HEIGHT` |  | screen height in pixels |
| `--dpi DPI` |  | screen density |
| `--fps FPS` |  | frames per second |
| `--tag TAG` |  | tag for selectors (repeatable) |
| `--data-volume VOLUME` |  | adopt an existing Docker volume as /data (one Android only) |
| `--image IMAGE` |  | run this exact image instead of the one for the Android version |

Example:

```
sf create -n 5 --android 13 --gpu igpu --tag eu
sf create --name shop --net vpn --vpn nl-ams.ovpn
```

## sf rm

Alias: `sf delete`.

Delete Androids and, unless --keep-data, their data. With backup.auto_before_risky (the default) a backup is taken first.

```
sf rm [--keep-data] [--force] [-y] selector
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--keep-data` |  | keep the /data volume (it can be adopted again later) |
| `--force` |  | delete even if the safety backup cannot be taken |
| `-y, --yes` |  | do not ask for confirmation |

Example:

```
sf rm 7
sf rm tag:test --keep-data --yes
```

## sf set

Change per-Android settings. Keys are InstanceSpec fields, nested ones with a dot (network.mode, resources.cpus, device.locale). Lists are comma separated. `default` puts an optional setting back to following the farm's value.

```
sf set [--force] selector key=value [key=value ...]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |
| `key=value` | one or more settings |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--force` |  | allow a change that can lose data (another Android version on existing data) |

Example:

```
sf set 1-5 fps=30 network.mode=vpn tags=eu,shop
sf set 3 gpu_mode=default
```

## sf info

```

```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Android id |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--device` |  | also ask the running Android about itself (model, build, battery) |

Example:

```

```

## sf logs

Show the container logs of one Android.

```
sf logs [-n LINES] [--logcat] id
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Android id |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-n, --lines LINES` | `200` | lines to show (default: 200) |
| `--logcat` |  | Android's own log (logcat) instead of the containers' output |

Example:

```

sf logs 3 --logcat
```

## sf gpu

GPUs and the rendering mode of Androids.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sf gpu ls` | list GPUs and the rendering choices on this machine |
| `sf gpu set` | choose how Androids draw (applied at their next restart) |

### sf gpu ls

List GPUs and the rendering choices on this machine.

```
sf gpu ls
```

Example:

```
sf gpu ls
```

### sf gpu set

Choose how Androids draw (applied at their next restart).

```
sf gpu set [--node DEVICE] selector {auto,software,igpu,dgpu,intel,amd,nvidia,default}
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |
| `{auto,software,igpu,dgpu,intel,amd,nvidia,default}` | `default` follows the farm's gpu.mode again |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--node DEVICE` |  | pin one card, e.g. /dev/dri/renderD129 (empty string: unpin) |

Example:

```
sf gpu set 1-8 igpu
sf gpu set 9 nvidia --node /dev/dri/renderD129
```

## sf tasks

List background tasks, or show, follow and cancel one.

```

```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | task id, e.g. t12 |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--active` |  | only tasks still running |
| `--cancel` |  | ask the task to stop |

Example:

```
sf tasks

```

```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

Print the panel's address and how to log in.

```

```

Example:

```
sf open
```

## sf shell

Run one command on every selected Android and show each one's output. The words after `--` are the command, passed as separate arguments (no shell on this machine ever sees them). Obviously destructive commands are refused unless --force.

```
sf shell [--root] [--timeout SECONDS] [--force] selector
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--root` |  | run as root inside the Android |
| `--timeout SECONDS` |  | time limit per Android (default: control.shell_timeout) |
| `--force` |  | run a command the safety denylist would refuse |

Example:

```
sf shell all -- getprop ro.build.version.release
sf shell 3 --root -- ls /data/app
```

## sf screenshot

```

```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Android id |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-o, --output FILE` |  | where to save (default: android-<id>.png) |

Example:

```
sf screenshot 3 -o shot.png
```

## sf apps

The app library: APK / XAPK / APKS / APKM files kept by the farm.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sf apps ls` | list the apps in the library |
| `sf apps add` | upload an app file into the library |
| `sf apps rm` | remove an app from the library |

### sf apps ls

List the apps in the library.

```
sf apps ls
```

Example:

```
sf apps ls
```

### sf apps add

Upload an app file into the library.

```
sf apps add FILE [FILE ...]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `FILE` | APK, XAPK, APKS or APKM file |

Example:

```
sf apps add ~/Downloads/shop-4.2.apk
```

### sf apps rm

Remove an app from the library.

```
sf apps rm app_id
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `app_id` | app id as shown by `sf apps ls` |

Example:

```
sf apps rm com.example.shop-42
```

## sf app

Apps on the Androids: install, launch, stop, clear, compare versions.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sf app install` | install an app from the library |
| `sf app ensure` | install an app only where it is missing or older |
| `sf app uninstall` | remove an app |
| `sf app launch` | open an app |
| `sf app stop` | force-stop an app |
| `sf app clear` | erase an app's data (as after a fresh install) |
| `sf app matrix` | which version of which app is installed where |

### sf app install

Install an app from the library.

```
sf app install [--no-grant] [--downgrade] selector app
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |
| `app` | app id from `sf apps ls`, or a package name (its newest version is used) |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--no-grant` |  | do not grant the app's runtime permissions |
| `--downgrade` |  | allow replacing a newer installed version |

Example:

```
sf app install 1-10 com.example.shop
```

### sf app ensure

Install an app only where it is missing or older.

```
sf app ensure [--no-grant] selector app
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |
| `app` | app id from `sf apps ls`, or a package name (its newest version is used) |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--no-grant` |  | do not grant the app's runtime permissions |

Example:

```
sf app ensure all com.example.shop
```

### sf app uninstall

Remove an app.

```
sf app uninstall [--keep-data] selector package
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |
| `package` | package name, e.g. com.example.shop |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--keep-data` |  | keep the app's data and cache |

Example:

```
sf app uninstall tag:test com.example.shop
```

### sf app launch

Open an app.

```
sf app launch selector package
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |
| `package` | package name, e.g. com.example.shop |

Example:

```
sf app launch all com.example.shop
```

### sf app stop

Force-stop an app.

```
sf app stop selector package
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |
| `package` | package name, e.g. com.example.shop |

Example:

```
sf app stop all com.example.shop
```

### sf app clear

Erase an app's data (as after a fresh install).

```
sf app clear selector package
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |
| `package` | package name, e.g. com.example.shop |

Example:

```
sf app clear 3 com.example.shop
```

### sf app matrix

Which version of which app is installed where.

```
sf app matrix [selector]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids (default: all) |

Example:

```
sf app matrix running
```

## sf push

Copy a local file onto Androids.

```
sf push selector local [remote]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |
| `local` | file on this machine |
| `remote` | folder (ending in /) or full path on the Android (default: /sdcard/Download/) |

Example:

```
sf push all notes.txt /sdcard/Download/
```

## sf pull

Copy a file from one Android to this machine.

```
sf pull [-o PATH] id remote
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Android id |
| `remote` | file path on the Android |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-o, --output PATH` |  | local file or folder (default: the file's name, here) |

Example:

```
sf pull 3 /sdcard/Download/report.pdf
```

## sf gallery

Add a picture or video to the gallery of Androids.

```
sf gallery selector local
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |
| `local` | picture or video on this machine |

Example:

```
sf gallery 1-5 photo.jpg
```

## sf input

Send the same touch or key to many Androids at once.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sf input tap` | tap a point of the screen |
| `sf input text` | type text into the focused field |
| `sf input key` | press a key |

### sf input tap

Tap one point on every selected Android. Coordinates are fractions of the screen (0.5 0.9 = centre, near the bottom), so one command fits every resolution.

```
sf input tap [--pixels] selector x y
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |
| `x` | 0 (left) to 1 (right) |
| `y` | 0 (top) to 1 (bottom) |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--pixels` |  | x and y are pixels, not fractions |

Example:

```
sf input tap 1-10 0.5 0.9
```

### sf input text

Type text into the focused field.

```
sf input text selector text
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |
| `text` | text to type (it appears in this machine's process list; never type secrets this way) |

Example:

```
sf input text 3 'hello world'
```

### sf input key

Press a key.

```
sf input key selector key
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |
| `key` | key name (HOME, BACK, ENTER, APP_SWITCH, ...) or an Android key code |

Example:

```
sf input key all HOME
```

## sf vpn

VPN profiles, logins and tunnel status.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sf vpn profiles` | list the imported VPN profiles |
| `sf vpn import` | import OpenVPN (.ovpn) or WireGuard (.conf) profiles |
| `sf vpn rm` | remove a VPN profile |
| `sf vpn credentials` | store the username and password a VPN profile logs in with |
| `sf vpn status` | tunnel state, public address and kill switch of Androids |

### sf vpn profiles

List the imported VPN profiles.

```
sf vpn profiles
```

Example:

```
sf vpn profiles
```

### sf vpn import

Import OpenVPN (.ovpn) or WireGuard (.conf) profiles.

```
sf vpn import FILE [FILE ...]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `FILE` |  |

Example:

```
sf vpn import ~/vpn/nl-ams.ovpn ~/vpn/de-fra.ovpn
```

### sf vpn rm

Remove a VPN profile.

```
sf vpn rm name
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | profile name as shown by `sf vpn profiles` |

Example:

```
sf vpn rm nl-ams.ovpn
```

### sf vpn credentials

Store a VPN login under a name (network.vpn.credentials says which name profiles use; `default` unless changed). The password is asked for without echo, or read from stdin with --password-stdin; it is never taken from the command line. Stored logins cannot be read back, only replaced or deleted. Without a name: list the names that exist.

```
sf vpn credentials [--username USERNAME] [--password-stdin] [--delete] [name]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | credentials name, e.g. default |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--username USERNAME` |  | VPN account name (asked for when omitted) |
| `--password-stdin` |  | read the password from stdin (one line) |
| `--delete` |  | delete the stored login |

Example:

```
sf vpn credentials default
printf '%s' "$VPN_PASSWORD" | sf vpn credentials default --username myaccount --password-stdin
```

### sf vpn status

Tunnel state, public address and kill switch of Androids.

```
sf vpn status [--refresh] [selector]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids (default: running) |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--refresh` |  | ask the public address again from inside each Android's network (a few seconds each) |

Example:

```
sf vpn status running
sf vpn status 3 --refresh
```

## sf gateway

Shared VPN gateways: one tunnel for many Androids.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sf gateway ls` | list gateways and their state |
| `sf gateway add` | define a gateway (or change an existing one) |
| `sf gateway rm` | remove a gateway (asks first) |
| `sf gateway up` | start a gateway and wait for its tunnel |
| `sf gateway down` | stop a gateway |

### sf gateway ls

List gateways and their state.

```
sf gateway ls
```

Example:

```
sf gateway ls
```

### sf gateway add

Define a gateway (or change an existing one).

```
sf gateway add --profile PROFILE [--provider {openvpn,wireguard}] [--credentials CREDENTIALS]
               [--subnet SUBNET]
               name
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | gateway name, e.g. eu |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--profile PROFILE` |  | VPN profile the gateway connects with |
| `--provider {openvpn,wireguard}` | `openvpn` |  |
| `--credentials CREDENTIALS` | `default` | credentials name (default: default) |
| `--subnet SUBNET` |  | private /24 for its Androids (default: next free one from docker.subnet_pool) |

Example:

```
sf gateway add eu --profile nl-ams.ovpn
```

### sf gateway rm

Remove a gateway (asks first).

```
sf gateway rm [--force] [-y] name
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `name` |  |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

## sf backup

Back up and restore Androids and the farm's settings.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sf backup create` | back up the data of Androids |
| `sf backup list` | list the backups |
| `sf backup verify` | check a backup against its recorded checksums |
| `sf backup restore` | restore a backup as a new Android, or over an existing one |
| `sf backup prune` | delete old backups, keeping the newest backup.keep of each Android |
| `sf backup farm` | back up the farm itself: settings, Android definitions, automation |

### sf backup create

Back up /data of every selected Android (tar + manifest with checksums). A running Android is stopped for the copy and started again when backup.stop_for_backup is on.

```
sf backup create selector
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `selector` | which Androids |

Example:

```
sf backup create 1-5
```

### sf backup list

Alias: `sf backup ls`.

List the backups.

```
sf backup list [--kind {android,farm,all}]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--kind {android,farm,all}` | `all` | which backups (default: all) |

Example:

```
sf backup list
```

### sf backup verify

Check a backup against its recorded checksums.

```
sf backup verify [--deep] archive
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `archive` | backup name as shown by `sf backup list` |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--deep` |  | also read the whole archive to check it can be unpacked |

Example:

```
sf backup verify android-3/20250101-040000
```

### sf backup restore

Without --over the backup becomes a NEW Android and nothing existing is touched. With --over ID that Android's data is replaced: it must be stopped, and you are asked first. A farm backup (farm/<time>) merges settings into this farm and never overwrites what exists. One this farm made itself is restored in full; from any other, only what cannot decide what runs on this machine is taken unless you say so with the flags below.

```
sf backup restore [--over ID] [--keep-network] [-y] [--trust] [--restore-config]
                  [--restore-secrets]
                  archive
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `archive` | backup name as shown by `sf backup list` |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--over ID` |  | replace the data of this existing Android (asks first) |
| `--keep-network` |  | restoring as new: keep the network on even though the original Android still exists |
| `-y, --yes` |  | do not ask for confirmation |
| `--trust` |  | farm backup from elsewhere: keep the Androids exactly as saved (custom image, data volume, boot arguments, autostart) and the schedules. Only for a backup you made yourself: it decides what runs on this machine with full privileges |
| `--restore-config` |  | farm backup from elsewhere: also take its config.yaml (never implied by --trust) |
| `--restore-secrets` |  | farm backup from elsewhere: also take its VPN profiles, logins and tokens |

Example:

```
sf backup restore android-3/20250101-040000
sf backup restore android-3/20250101-040000 --over 3
sf backup restore farm/20250101-050000
```

### sf backup prune

Delete old backups, keeping the newest backup.keep of each Android.

```
sf backup prune
```

Example:

```
sf backup prune
```

### sf backup farm

Back up the farm itself: settings, Android definitions, automation.

```
sf backup farm [--include-secrets]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--include-secrets` |  | also store VPN logins and tokens (the archive is then owner-only; keep it private) |

Example:

```
sf backup farm
```

With --http it serves Streamable HTTP on this machine only. Actions that change the farm follow ai.policy and wait for your Yes or No (sf approvals). Details: docs/MCP.md.

| Command | What it does |

| `sf mcp tools` | list the tools an assistant gets, with their class and what the policy does |

| --- | --- | --- |
| `--http` |  | the snippet for the HTTP endpoint instead of stdio |

sf mcp config --http
```

| --- | --- | --- |
| `--markdown` |  | print the tool reference as Markdown (docs/MCP.md is built from it) |

Example:

```
sf mcp tools
sf mcp tools --markdown
```

## sf ask

Send one request to the farm's built-in Assistant and print its steps and its answer. Actions that change the farm follow ai.policy: under `ask` each one is shown and waits for y or n here (or in the panel). The last line is the farm's own record of what ran.

```

| `--keep` |  | keep the conversation afterwards (see: sf ai conversations) |

```

#### sf ai models add

Add or replace a profile.

```

                 [--key-name KEY_NAME] [--vision] [--no-tools] [--timeout TIMEOUT] [--default]
                 name
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | profile name: lower-case letters, digits, - and _ |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--provider {ollama,openai}` |  | wire format: an Ollama server, or any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API |
| `--base-url BASE_URL` |  | server address (default: http://127.0.0.1:11434) |
| `--model MODEL` |  | model name on that server (default: the first it lists) |

### sf ai pilot

With a goal: start a Pilot session on the selected Androids. A model operates the app one action at a time and every action is recorded; a run counts only when the success check really holds. Train the recordings (--train, or `sf ai pilot train`) into a program that replays with no model: sf auto run program <dataset> <selector>.

With a word: sessions | show <session> | cancel <session> | resolve <session> <android> resume|skip|abort | confirm <session> <android> | train <dataset>.

```
sf ai pilot [--app PACKAGE] [--success CHECK] [--runs RUNS] [--model MODEL]
            [--max-steps MAX_STEPS] [--dataset DATASET] [--value NAME=VALUE] [--ask-value NAME]
            [--train] [--steps]
            GOAL SELECTOR | WORD ... [GOAL SELECTOR | WORD ... ...]
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `GOAL SELECTOR | WORD ...` | "<goal>" <selector> to start a session, or: sessions \| show \| cancel \| resolve \| confirm \| train |

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--app PACKAGE` |  | the app to operate, e.g. com.android.settings |
| `--success CHECK` |  | what must be on screen when the goal is reached: text:..., id:..., desc:..., package:... or activity:... (without it a run can only be checked by the model's own evidence) |
| `--runs RUNS` | `1` | runs per Android (default: 1; three or more give a real consensus) |
| `--model MODEL` |  | model profile to use (default: ai.default_model) |
| `--max-steps MAX_STEPS` |  | actions per run (default: ai.pilot.max_steps) |
| `--dataset DATASET` |  | dataset to record into (default: named after the goal) |
| `--value NAME=VALUE` |  | a value the Pilot may type by name (kept in memory for this session only) |
| `--ask-value NAME` |  | like --value, but the value is asked for here without being shown (use it for secrets) |
| `--train` |  | train the dataset when the session ends with verified runs |
| `--steps` |  | with `show`: list every action and the model's reason for it |

Example:

```
sf ai pilot "open the date and time settings" 1 --app com.android.settings --success "text:Set time automatically" --runs 3 --train
sf ai pilot sessions
sf ai pilot show t12 --steps
sf ai pilot resolve t12 3 resume
sf ai pilot confirm t12 3
sf ai pilot train open-the-date-and-time-settings
```

Show every command host setup would run, changing nothing.

```
sf host plan [--boot]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--boot` |  | only what must be redone after every reboot |

Example:

```
sf host plan
```

### sf host apply

Install packages, load kernel modules, raise kernel limits, create runtime folders and install the systemd units. Needs root: started as a normal user it continues under sudo, keeping your farm home. Safe to repeat.

```
sf host apply [--dry-run] [--boot]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` |  | print every command and file, change nothing |
| `--boot` |  | only what must be redone after every reboot |

Example:

```
sf host apply
sf host apply --dry-run
```

### sf host capacity

Estimate how many Androids this machine can run at once.

```
sf host capacity [--workload {video,light}]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--workload {video,light}` | `video` | video: apps playing video, the heaviest case measured (default). light: mostly idle screens |

Example:

```
sf host capacity
```

### sf host gpus

List the GPUs found and the rendering modes they allow.

```
sf host gpus
```

Example:

```
sf host gpus
```

### sf host sign-module

Run scripts/host/sign-module.sh. Without arguments it reports the Secure Boot state and the signing key in use. Arguments after `--` go to the script (see its --help); anything but a status report runs under sudo.

```
sf host sign-module
```

Example:

```
sf host sign-module                              (status report)
sf host sign-module -- --create-key --enroll v4l2loopback
```

## sf config

Read and change the farm's settings (config.yaml).

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sf config get` | print one setting |
| `sf config set` | change one setting (validated before it is saved) |
| `sf config unset` | put one setting back to its default |
| `sf config show` | print all settings in effect |
| `sf config path` | print where config.yaml is |
| `sf config docs` | render the settings reference (docs/CONFIGURATION.md) |

### sf config get

Print one setting.

```
sf config get key
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `key` | dotted key, e.g. network.vpn.selection |

Example:

```
sf config get android.fps
```

### sf config set

Change one setting (validated before it is saved).

```
sf config set key value
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `key` | dotted key, e.g. android.fps |
| `value` | new value; lists are comma separated |

Example:

```
sf config set android.fps 25
sf config set network.dns 1.1.1.1,9.9.9.9
```

### sf config unset

Put one setting back to its default.

```
sf config unset key
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `key` | dotted key |

Example:

```
sf config unset android.fps
```

### sf config show

Print all settings in effect.

```
sf config show [--changed]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--changed` |  | only what differs from the defaults (the file's content) |

Example:

```
sf config show --changed
```

### sf config path

Print where config.yaml is.

```
sf config path
```

Example:

```
sf config path
```

### sf config docs

Render the settings reference (docs/CONFIGURATION.md).

```
sf config docs [-o FILE] [--check FILE]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-o, --output FILE` |  | write to FILE instead of printing |
| `--check FILE` |  | exit 1 when FILE differs from what would be generated (for CI) |

Example:

```
sf config docs -o docs/CONFIGURATION.md
sf config docs --check docs/CONFIGURATION.md
```

## sf token

Print the API token the panel and scripts log in with.

```
sf token [--rotate]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--rotate` |  | replace the token; the old one stops working at once |

Example:

```
sf token
sf token --rotate
```

## sf serve

Run the daemon in the foreground until Ctrl-C. Androids keep running when it stops.

```
sf serve [--host HOST] [--port PORT]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--host HOST` |  | listen address (default: server.host, 127.0.0.1) |
| `--port PORT` |  | listen port (default: server.port, 7700) |

Example:

```
sf serve
sf serve --port 7701
```

## sf service

Run the daemon as a systemd user service.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sf service install` | write and enable the user service |
| `sf service start` | start the daemon in the background |
| `sf service stop` | stop the daemon (Androids keep running) |
| `sf service status` | show whether the daemon runs |
| `sf service logs` | show the daemon's log |

### sf service install

Write and enable the user service.

```
sf service install
```

Example:

```
sf service install
```

### sf service start

Start the daemon in the background.

```
sf service start
```

Example:

```
sf service start
```

### sf service stop

Stop the daemon (Androids keep running).

```
sf service stop
```

Example:

```
sf service stop
```

### sf service status

Show whether the daemon runs.

```
sf service status
```

Example:

```
sf service status
```

### sf service logs

Show the daemon's log.

```
sf service logs [-n LINES] [-f]
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-n, --lines LINES` | `100` | lines to show (default: 100) |
| `-f, --follow` |  | keep printing new lines |

Example:

```
sf service logs -f
```

## sf version

Print the version.

```
sf version
```

Example:

```
sf version
```

## sf completion

Print a shell completion script.

```
sf completion {bash,zsh}
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `{bash,zsh}` |  |

Example:

```
sf completion bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/sf
sf completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_sf
```
